    83→def compute_embeddings_via_server(chunks: list[str], model_name: str, port: int) -> np.ndarray:
    84→    """Computes embeddings using sentence-transformers.
    85→
    86→    Args:
    87→        chunks: List of text chunks to embed
    88→        model_name: Name of the sentence transformer model
    89→    """
    90→    logger.info(
    91→        f"Computing embeddings for {len(chunks)} chunks using SentenceTransformer model '{model_name}' (via embedding server)..."
    92→    )
    93→    import msgpack
    94→    import numpy as np
    95→    import zmq
    96→
    97→    # Connect to embedding server
    98→    context = zmq.Context()
    99→    socket = context.socket(zmq.REQ)
   100→    socket.connect(f"tcp://localhost:{port}")
   101→
   102→    # Send chunks to server for embedding computation
   103→    request = chunks
   104→    socket.send(msgpack.packb(request))
   105→
   106→    # Receive embeddings from server
   107→    response = socket.recv()
   108→    embeddings_list = msgpack.unpackb(response)
   109→
   110→    # Convert back to numpy array
   111→    embeddings = np.array(embeddings_list, dtype=np.float32)
   112→
   113→    socket.close()
   114→    context.term()
   115→
   116→    return embeddings

   128→    def __init__(
   129→        self, passage_sources: list[dict[str, Any]], metadata_file_path: Optional[str] = None
   130→    ):
   131→        self.offset_maps: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
   132→        self.passage_files: dict[str, str] = {}
   133→        # Avoid materializing a single gigantic global map to reduce memory
   134→        # footprint on very large corpora (e.g., 60M+ passages). Instead, keep
   135→        # per-shard maps and do a lightweight per-shard lookup on demand.
   136→        self._total_count: int = 0
   137→        self.filter_engine = MetadataFilterEngine()  # Initialize filter engine
   138→
   139→        # Derive index base name for standard sibling fallbacks, e.g., <index_name>.passages.*
   140→        index_name_base = None
   141→        if metadata_file_path:
   142→            meta_name = Path(metadata_file_path).name
   143→            if meta_name.endswith(".meta.json"):
   144→                index_name_base = meta_name[: -len(".meta.json")]
   145→
   146→        for source in passage_sources:
   147→            assert source["type"] == "jsonl", "only jsonl is supported"
   148→            passage_file = source.get("path", "")
   149→            index_file = source.get("index_path", "")  # .idx file
   150→
   151→            # Fix path resolution - relative paths should be relative to metadata file directory
   152→            def _resolve_candidates(
   153→                primary: str,
   154→                relative_key: str,
   155→                default_name: Optional[str],
   156→                source_dict: dict[str, Any],
   157→            ) -> list[Path]:
   158→                """
   159→                Build an ordered list of candidate paths. For relative paths specified in
   160→                metadata, prefer resolution relative to the metadata file directory first,
   161→                then fall back to CWD-based resolution, and finally to conventional
   162→                sibling defaults (e.g., <index_base>.passages.idx / .jsonl).
   163→                """
   164→                candidates: list[Path] = []
   165→                # 1) Primary path
   166→                if primary:
   167→                    p = Path(primary)
   168→                    if p.is_absolute():
   169→                        candidates.append(p)
   170→                    else:
   171→                        # Prefer metadata-relative resolution for relative paths
   172→                        if metadata_file_path:
   173→                            candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / p)
   174→                        # Also consider CWD-relative as a fallback for legacy layouts
   175→                        candidates.append(Path.cwd() / p)
   176→                # 2) metadata-relative explicit relative key (if present)
   177→                if metadata_file_path and source_dict.get(relative_key):
   178→                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / source_dict[relative_key])
   179→                # 3) metadata-relative standard sibling filename
   180→                if metadata_file_path and default_name:
   181→                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / default_name)
   182→                return candidates
   183→
   184→            # Build candidate lists and pick first existing; otherwise keep last candidate for error message
   185→            idx_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.idx" if index_name_base else None
   186→            idx_candidates = _resolve_candidates(
   187→                index_file, "index_path_relative", idx_default, source
   188→            )
   189→            pas_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.jsonl" if index_name_base else None
   190→            pas_candidates = _resolve_candidates(passage_file, "path_relative", pas_default, source)
   191→
   192→            def _pick_existing(cands: list[Path]) -> str:
   193→                for c in cands:
   194→                    if c.exists():
   195→                        return str(c.resolve())
   196→                # Fallback to last candidate (best guess) even if not exists; will error below
   197→                return str(cands[-1].resolve()) if cands else ""
   198→
   199→            index_file = _pick_existing(idx_candidates)
   200→            passage_file = _pick_existing(pas_candidates)
   201→
   202→            if not Path(index_file).exists():
   203→                raise FileNotFoundError(f"Passage index file not found: {index_file}")
   204→
   205→            with open(index_file, "rb") as f:
   206→                offset_map: dict[str, int] = pickle.load(f)
   207→                self.offset_maps[passage_file] = offset_map
   208→                self.passage_files[passage_file] = passage_file
   209→                self._total_count += len(offset_map)

   211→    def get_passage(self, passage_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   212→        # Fast path: check each shard map (there are typically few shards).
   213→        # This avoids building a massive combined dict while keeping lookups
   214→        # bounded by the number of shards.
   215→        for passage_file, offset_map in self.offset_maps.items():
   216→            try:
   217→                offset = offset_map[passage_id]
   218→                with open(passage_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   219→                    f.seek(offset)
   220→                    return json.loads(f.readline())
   221→            except KeyError:
   222→                continue
   223→        raise KeyError(f"Passage ID not found: {passage_id}")

   225→    def filter_search_results(
   226→        self,
   227→        search_results: list[SearchResult],
   228→        metadata_filters: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, Union[str, int, float, bool, list]]]],
   229→    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
   230→        """
   231→        Apply metadata filters to search results.
   232→
   233→        Args:
   234→            search_results: List of SearchResult objects
   235→            metadata_filters: Filter specifications to apply
   236→
   237→        Returns:
   238→            Filtered list of SearchResult objects
   239→        """
   240→        if not metadata_filters:
   241→            return search_results
   242→
   243→        logger.debug(f"Applying metadata filters to {len(search_results)} results")
   244→
   245→        # Convert SearchResult objects to dictionaries for the filter engine
   246→        result_dicts = []
   247→        for result in search_results:
   248→            result_dicts.append(
   249→                {
   250→                    "id": result.id,
   251→                    "score": result.score,
   252→                    "text": result.text,
   253→                    "metadata": result.metadata,
   254→                }
   255→            )
   256→
   257→        # Apply filters using the filter engine
   258→        filtered_dicts = self.filter_engine.apply_filters(result_dicts, metadata_filters)
   259→
   260→        # Convert back to SearchResult objects
   261→        filtered_results = []
   262→        for result_dict in filtered_dicts:
   263→            filtered_results.append(
   264→                SearchResult(
   265→                    id=result_dict["id"],
   266→                    score=result_dict["score"],
   267→                    text=result_dict["text"],
   268→                    metadata=result_dict["metadata"],
   269→                )
   270→            )
   271→
   272→        logger.debug(f"Filtered results: {len(filtered_results)} remaining")
   273→        return filtered_results

    12→class BaseSearcher(LeannBackendSearcherInterface, ABC):
    13→    """
    14→    Abstract base class for Leann searchers, containing common logic for
    15→    loading metadata, managing embedding servers, and handling file paths.
    16→    """
    17→
    18→    def __init__(self, index_path: str, backend_module_name: str, **kwargs):
    19→        """
    20→        Initializes the BaseSearcher.
    21→
    22→        Args:
    23→            index_path: Path to the Leann index file (e.g., '.../my_index.leann').
    24→            backend_module_name: The specific embedding server module to use
    25→                                 (e.g., 'leann_backend_hnsw.hnsw_embedding_server').
    26→            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments.
    27→        """
    28→        self.index_path = Path(index_path)
    29→        self.index_dir = self.index_path.parent
    30→        self.meta = kwargs.get("meta", self._load_meta())
    31→
    32→        if not self.meta:
    33→            raise ValueError("Searcher requires metadata from .meta.json.")
    34→
    35→        self.dimensions = self.meta.get("dimensions")
    36→        if not self.dimensions:
    37→            raise ValueError("Dimensions not found in Leann metadata.")
    38→
    39→        self.embedding_model = self.meta.get("embedding_model")
    40→        if not self.embedding_model:
    41→            print("WARNING: embedding_model not found in meta.json. Recompute will fail.")
    42→
    43→        self.embedding_mode = self.meta.get("embedding_mode", "sentence-transformers")
    44→        self.embedding_options = self.meta.get("embedding_options", {})
    45→
    46→        self.embedding_server_manager = EmbeddingServerManager(
    47→            backend_module_name=backend_module_name,
    48→        )

    50→    def _load_meta(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    51→        """Loads the metadata file associated with the index."""
    52→        # This is the corrected logic for finding the meta file.
    53→        meta_path = self.index_dir / f"{self.index_path.name}.meta.json"
    54→        if not meta_path.exists():
    55→            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Leann metadata file not found at {meta_path}")
    56→        with open(meta_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
    57→            return json.load(f)

    59→    def _ensure_server_running(
    60→        self, passages_source_file: str, port: Optional[int], **kwargs

    64→        This is a helper for subclasses.
    65→        """
    66→        if not self.embedding_model:

    69→        # Get distance_metric from meta if not provided in kwargs

    89→            passages_file=passages_source_file,

    99→    def compute_query_embedding(
   100→        self,
   101→        query: str,
   102→        use_server_if_available: bool = True,
   103→        zmq_port: Optional[int] = None,
   104→        query_template: Optional[str] = None,
   105→    ) -> np.ndarray:
   106→        """
   107→        Compute embedding for a query string.
   108→
   109→        Args:
   110→            query: The query string to embed
   111→            zmq_port: ZMQ port for embedding server
   112→            use_server_if_available: Whether to try using embedding server first
   113→            query_template: Optional prompt template to prepend to query
   114→
   115→        Returns:
   116→            Query embedding as numpy array
   117→        """
   118→        # Apply query template BEFORE any computation path
   119→        # This ensures template is applied consistently for both server and fallback paths
   120→        if query_template:
   121→            query = f"{query_template}{query}"
   122→
   123→        # Try to use embedding server if available and requested
   124→        if use_server_if_available:
   125→            try:
   126→                # TODO: Maybe we can directly use this port here?
   127→                # For this internal method, it's ok to assume that the server is running
   128→                # on that port?
   129→
   130→                # Ensure we have a server with passages_file for compatibility
   131→                passages_source_file = self.index_dir / f"{self.index_path.name}.meta.json"
   132→                # Convert to absolute path to ensure server can find it
   133→                zmq_port = self._ensure_server_running(
   134→                    str(passages_source_file.resolve()), zmq_port
   135→                )
   136→
   137→                return self._compute_embedding_via_server([query], zmq_port)[
   138→                    0:1
   139→                ]  # Return (1, D) shape
   140→            except Exception as e:
   141→                print(f"⚠️ Embedding server failed: {e}")
   142→                print("⏭️ Falling back to direct model loading...")
   143→
   144→        # Fallback to direct computation
   145→        from .embedding_compute import compute_embeddings
   146→
   147→        embedding_mode = self.meta.get("embedding_mode", "sentence-transformers")
   148→        return compute_embeddings(
   149→            [query],
   150→            self.embedding_model,
   151→            embedding_mode,
   152→            provider_options=self.embedding_options,
   153→        )

   155→    def _compute_embedding_via_server(self, chunks: list, zmq_port: int) -> np.ndarray:
   156→        """Compute embeddings using the ZMQ embedding server."""
   157→        import msgpack
   158→        import zmq
   159→
   160→        try:
   161→            context = zmq.Context()
   162→            socket = context.socket(zmq.REQ)
   163→            socket.setsockopt(zmq.RCVTIMEO, 30000)  # 30 second timeout
   164→            socket.connect(f"tcp://localhost:{zmq_port}")
   165→
   166→            # Send embedding request
   167→            request = chunks
   168→            request_bytes = msgpack.packb(request)
   169→            socket.send(request_bytes)
   170→
   171→            # Wait for response
   172→            response_bytes = socket.recv()
   173→            response = msgpack.unpackb(response_bytes)
   174→
   175→            socket.close()
   176→            context.term()
   177→
   178→            # Convert response to numpy array
   179→            if isinstance(response, list) and len(response) > 0:
   180→                return np.array(response, dtype=np.float32)
   181→            else:
   182→                raise RuntimeError("Invalid response from embedding server")
   183→
   184→        except Exception as e:
   185→            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to compute embeddings via server: {e}")

   199→    ) -> dict[str, Any]:

   205→            top_k: Number of nearest neighbors to return
   206→            complexity: Search complexity/candidate list size, higher = more accurate but slower
   207→            beam_width: Number of parallel search paths/IO requests per iteration
   208→            prune_ratio: Ratio of neighbors to prune via approximate distance (0.0-1.0)
   209→            recompute_embeddings: Whether to fetch fresh embeddings from server vs use stored PQ codes
   210→            pruning_strategy: PQ candidate selection strategy - "global" (default), "local", or "proportional"
   211→            zmq_port: ZMQ port for embedding server communication. Must be provided if recompute_embeddings is True.
   212→            **kwargs: Backend-specific parameters (e.g., batch_size, dedup_node_dis, etc.)
   213→
   214→        Returns:
   215→            Dict with 'labels' (list of lists) and 'distances' (ndarray)
   216→        """

   314→            ("openai", "text-embedding-ada-002"),
   315→            ("openai", "text-embedding-3-small"),
   316→            ("openai", "text-embedding-3-large"),
   317→            # Voyage AI models
   318→            ("voyage", "voyage-2"),
   319→            ("voyage", "voyage-3"),
   320→            ("voyage", "voyage-large-2"),
   321→            ("voyage", "voyage-multilingual-2"),
   322→            ("voyage", "voyage-code-2"),
   323→            # Cohere models
   324→            ("cohere", "embed-english-v3.0"),
   325→            ("cohere", "embed-multilingual-v3.0"),
   326→            ("cohere", "embed-english-light-v3.0"),
   327→            ("cohere", "embed-multilingual-light-v3.0"),
   328→        }
   329→

   331→        is_normalized = False
   332→        current_model_lower = embedding_model.lower()
   333→        current_mode_lower = embedding_mode.lower()
   334→
   335→        # Check exact matches
   336→        for mode, model in normalized_embeddings_models:

   338→                mode in current_mode_lower and model in current_model_lower

    36→    @abstractmethod

    61→            complexity: Search complexity/candidate list size, higher = more accurate but slower
    62→            beam_width: Number of parallel search paths/IO requests per iteration
    63→            prune_ratio: Ratio of neighbors to prune via approximate distance (0.0-1.0)
    64→            recompute_embeddings: Whether to fetch fresh embeddings from server vs use stored PQ codes
    65→            pruning_strategy: PQ candidate selection strategy - "global" (default), "local", or "proportional"

    69→        Returns:

content.content:
1→"""
     2→Metadata filtering engine for LEANN search results.
     3→
     4→This module provides generic metadata filtering capabilities that can be applied
     5→to search results from any LEANN backend. The filtering supports various
     6→operators for different data types including numbers, strings, booleans, and lists.
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→from typing import Any, Optional, Union
    11→
    12→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    13→
    14→# Type alias for filter specifications
    15→FilterValue = Union[str, int, float, bool, list]
    16→FilterSpec = dict[str, FilterValue]
    17→MetadataFilters = dict[str, FilterSpec]
    18→
    19→
    20→class MetadataFilterEngine:
    21→    """
    22→    Engine for evaluating metadata filters against search results.
    23→
    24→    Supports various operators for filtering based on metadata fields:
    25→    - Comparison: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=
    26→    - Membership: in, not_in
    27→    - String operations: contains, starts_with, ends_with
    28→    - Boolean operations: is_true, is_false
    29→    """
    30→
    31→    def __init__(self):
    32→        """Initialize the filter engine with supported operators."""
    33→        self.operators = {
    34→            "==": self._equals,
    35→            "!=": self._not_equals,
    36→            "<": self._less_than,
    37→            "<=": self._less_than_or_equal,
    38→            ">": self._greater_than,
    39→            ">=": self._greater_than_or_equal,
    40→            "in": self._in,
    41→            "not_in": self._not_in,
    42→            "contains": self._contains,
    43→            "starts_with": self._starts_with,
    44→            "ends_with": self._ends_with,
    45→            "is_true": self._is_true,
    46→            "is_false": self._is_false,
    47→        }
    48→
    49→    def apply_filters(
    50→        self, search_results: list[dict[str, Any]], metadata_filters: Optional[MetadataFilters]
    51→    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    52→        """
    53→        Apply metadata filters to a list of search results.
    54→
    55→        Args:
    56→            search_results: List of result dictionaries, each containing 'metadata' field
    57→            metadata_filters: Dictionary of filter specifications
    58→                Format: {"field_name": {"operator": value}}
    59→
    60→        Returns:
    61→            Filtered list of search results
    62→        """
    63→        if not metadata_filters:
    64→            return search_results
    65→
    66→        logger.debug(f"Applying filters: {metadata_filters}")
    67→        logger.debug(f"Input results count: {len(search_results)}")
    68→
    69→        filtered_results = []
    70→        for result in search_results:
    71→            if self._evaluate_filters(result, metadata_filters):
    72→                filtered_results.append(result)
    73→
    74→        logger.debug(f"Filtered results count: {len(filtered_results)}")
    75→        return filtered_results
    76→
    77→    def _evaluate_filters(self, result: dict[str, Any], filters: MetadataFilters) -> bool:
    78→        """
    79→        Evaluate all filters against a single search result.
    80→
    81→        All filters must pass (AND logic) for the result to be included.
    82→
    83→        Args:
    84→            result: Full search result dictionary (including metadata, text, etc.)
    85→            filters: Filter specifications to evaluate
    86→
    87→        Returns:
    88→            True if all filters pass, False otherwise
    89→        """
    90→        for field_name, filter_spec in filters.items():
    91→            if not self._evaluate_field_filter(result, field_name, filter_spec):
    92→                return False
    93→        return True
    94→
    95→    def _evaluate_field_filter(
    96→        self, result: dict[str, Any], field_name: str, filter_spec: FilterSpec
    97→    ) -> bool:
    98→        """
    99→        Evaluate a single field filter against a search result.
   100→
   101→        Args:
   102→            result: Full search result dictionary
   103→            field_name: Name of the field to filter on
   104→            filter_spec: Filter specification for this field
   105→
   106→        Returns:
   107→            True if the filter passes, False otherwise
   108→        """
   109→        # First check top-level fields, then check metadata
   110→        field_value = result.get(field_name)
   111→        if field_value is None:
   112→            # Try to get from metadata if not found at top level
   113→            metadata = result.get("metadata", {})
   114→            field_value = metadata.get(field_name)
   115→
   116→        # Handle missing fields - they fail all filters except existence checks
   117→        if field_value is None:
   118→            logger.debug(f"Field '{field_name}' not found in result or metadata")
   119→            return False
   120→
   121→        # Evaluate each operator in the filter spec
   122→        for operator, expected_value in filter_spec.items():
   123→            if operator not in self.operators:
   124→                logger.warning(f"Unsupported operator: {operator}")
   125→                return False
   126→
   127→            try:
   128→                if not self.operators[operator](field_value, expected_value):
   129→                    logger.debug(
   130→                        f"Filter failed: {field_name} {operator} {expected_value} "
   131→                        f"(actual: {field_value})"
   132→                    )
   133→                    return False
   134→            except Exception as e:
   135→                logger.warning(
   136→                    f"Error evaluating filter {field_name} {operator} {expected_value}: {e}"
   137→                )
   138→                return False
   139→
   140→        return True
   141→
   142→    # Comparison operators
   143→    def _equals(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   144→        """Check if field value equals expected value."""
   145→        return field_value == expected_value
   146→
   147→    def _not_equals(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   148→        """Check if field value does not equal expected value."""
   149→        return field_value != expected_value
   150→
   151→    def _less_than(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   152→        """Check if field value is less than expected value."""
   153→        return self._numeric_compare(field_value, expected_value, lambda a, b: a < b)
   154→
   155→    def _less_than_or_equal(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   156→        """Check if field value is less than or equal to expected value."""
   157→        return self._numeric_compare(field_value, expected_value, lambda a, b: a <= b)
   158→
   159→    def _greater_than(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   160→        """Check if field value is greater than expected value."""
   161→        return self._numeric_compare(field_value, expected_value, lambda a, b: a > b)
   162→
   163→    def _greater_than_or_equal(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   164→        """Check if field value is greater than or equal to expected value."""
   165→        return self._numeric_compare(field_value, expected_value, lambda a, b: a >= b)
   166→
   167→    # Membership operators
   168→    def _in(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   169→        """Check if field value is in the expected list/collection."""
   170→        if not isinstance(expected_value, (list, tuple, set)):
   171→            raise ValueError("'in' operator requires a list, tuple, or set")
   172→        return field_value in expected_value
   173→
   174→    def _not_in(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   175→        """Check if field value is not in the expected list/collection."""
   176→        if not isinstance(expected_value, (list, tuple, set)):
   177→            raise ValueError("'not_in' operator requires a list, tuple, or set")
   178→        return field_value not in expected_value
   179→
   180→    # String operators
   181→    def _contains(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   182→        """Check if field value contains the expected substring."""
   183→        field_str = str(field_value)
   184→        expected_str = str(expected_value)
   185→        return expected_str in field_str
   186→
   187→    def _starts_with(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   188→        """Check if field value starts with the expected prefix."""
   189→        field_str = str(field_value)
   190→        expected_str = str(expected_value)
   191→        return field_str.startswith(expected_str)
   192→
   193→    def _ends_with(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   194→        """Check if field value ends with the expected suffix."""
   195→        field_str = str(field_value)
   196→        expected_str = str(expected_value)
   197→        return field_str.endswith(expected_str)
   198→
   199→    # Boolean operators
   200→    def _is_true(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   201→        """Check if field value is truthy."""
   202→        return bool(field_value)
   203→
   204→    def _is_false(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   205→        """Check if field value is falsy."""
   206→        return not bool(field_value)
   207→
   208→    # Helper methods
   209→    def _numeric_compare(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any, compare_func) -> bool:
   210→        """
   211→        Helper for numeric comparisons with type coercion.
   212→
   213→        Args:
   214→            field_value: Value from metadata
   215→            expected_value: Value to compare against
   216→            compare_func: Comparison function to apply
   217→
   218→        Returns:
   219→            Result of comparison
   220→        """
   221→        try:
   222→            # Try to convert both values to numbers for comparison
   223→            if isinstance(field_value, str) and isinstance(expected_value, str):
   224→                # String comparison if both are strings
   225→                return compare_func(field_value, expected_value)
   226→
   227→            # Numeric comparison - attempt to convert to float
   228→            field_num = (
   229→                float(field_value) if not isinstance(field_value, (int, float)) else field_value
   230→            )
   231→            expected_num = (
   232→                float(expected_value)
   233→                if not isinstance(expected_value, (int, float))
   234→                else expected_value
   235→            )
   236→
   237→            return compare_func(field_num, expected_num)
   238→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   239→            # Fall back to string comparison if numeric conversion fails
   240→            return compare_func(str(field_value), str(expected_value))
   241→

   189→            pas_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.jsonl" if index_name_base else None
   190→            pas_candidates = _resolve_candidates(passage_file, "path_relative", pas_default, source)
   191→
   192→            def _pick_existing(cands: list[Path]) -> str:
   193→                for c in cands:
   194→                    if c.exists():
   195→                        return str(c.resolve())
   196→                # Fallback to last candidate (best guess) even if not exists; will error below
   197→                return str(cands[-1].resolve()) if cands else ""
   198→
   199→            index_file = _pick_existing(idx_candidates)
   200→            passage_file = _pick_existing(pas_candidates)
   201→
   202→            if not Path(index_file).exists():

   204→
   205→            with open(index_file, "rb") as f:
   206→                offset_map: dict[str, int] = pickle.load(f)
   207→                self.offset_maps[passage_file] = offset_map
   208→                self.passage_files[passage_file] = passage_file
   209→                self._total_count += len(offset_map)

   211→    def get_passage(self, passage_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   212→        # Fast path: check each shard map (there are typically few shards).
   213→        # This avoids building a massive combined dict while keeping lookups
   214→        # bounded by the number of shards.
   215→        for passage_file, offset_map in self.offset_maps.items():
   216→            try:
   217→                offset = offset_map[passage_id]
   218→                with open(passage_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   219→                    f.seek(offset)
   220→                    return json.loads(f.readline())
   221→            except KeyError:
   222→                continue

   225→    def filter_search_results(
   226→        self,
   227→        search_results: list[SearchResult],
   228→        metadata_filters: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, Union[str, int, float, bool, list]]]],
   229→    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
   230→        """

   237→        Returns:

   240→        if not metadata_filters:
   241→            return search_results
   242→
   243→        logger.debug(f"Applying metadata filters to {len(search_results)} results")
   244→
   245→        # Convert SearchResult objects to dictionaries for the filter engine
   246→        result_dicts = []
   247→        for result in search_results:
   248→            result_dicts.append(
   249→                {
   250→                    "id": result.id,
   251→                    "score": result.score,

   256→
   257→        # Apply filters using the filter engine
   258→        filtered_dicts = self.filter_engine.apply_filters(result_dicts, metadata_filters)
   259→
   260→        # Convert back to SearchResult objects
   261→        filtered_results = []
   262→        for result_dict in filtered_dicts:

   729→            embeddings = embeddings / norms
   730→
   731→        index = faiss.read_index(str(index_file))
   732→        if hasattr(index, "is_recompute"):
   733→            index.is_recompute = needs_recompute
   734→            print(f"index.is_recompute: {index.is_recompute}")
   735→        if getattr(index, "storage", None) is None:
   736→            if index.metric_type == faiss.METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT:
   737→                storage_index = faiss.IndexFlatIP(index.d)
   738→            else:
   739→                storage_index = faiss.IndexFlatL2(index.d)
   740→            index.storage = storage_index

   743→            # population (even if the vectors themselves were pruned from disk
   744→            # for recompute mode).  When we attach a fresh IndexFlat here its
   745→            # ntotal starts at zero, which later causes IndexHNSW::add to
   746→            # believe new "preset" levels were provided and trips the
   747→            # `n0 + n == levels.size()` assertion.  Seed the temporary storage
   748→            # with the current ntotal so Faiss maintains the proper offset for
   749→            # incoming vectors.
   750→            try:
   751→                storage_index.ntotal = index.ntotal
   752→            except AttributeError:
   753→                # Older Faiss builds may not expose ntotal as a writable
   754→                # attribute; in that case we fall back to the default behaviour.
   755→                pass
   756→        if index.d != embedding_dim:
   757→            raise ValueError(
   758→                f"Existing index dimension ({index.d}) does not match new embeddings ({embedding_dim})."
   759→            )
   760→
   761→        passage_meta_mode = meta.get("embedding_mode", self.embedding_mode)
   762→        passage_provider_options = meta.get("embedding_options", self.embedding_options)
   763→
   764→        base_id = index.ntotal
   765→        for offset, chunk in enumerate(valid_chunks):
   766→            new_id = str(base_id + offset)
   767→            chunk.setdefault("metadata", {})["id"] = new_id
   768→            chunk["id"] = new_id
   769→
   770→        # Append passages/offsets before we attempt index.add so the ZMQ server
   771→        # can resolve newly assigned IDs during recompute. Keep rollback hooks
   772→        # so we can restore files if the update fails mid-way.
   773→        rollback_passages_size = passages_file.stat().st_size if passages_file.exists() else 0
   774→        offset_map_backup = offset_map.copy()
   775→
   776→        try:
   777→            with open(passages_file, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   778→                for chunk in valid_chunks:
   779→                    offset = f.tell()
   780→                    json.dump(
   781→                        {
   782→                            "id": chunk["id"],
   783→                            "text": chunk["text"],
   784→                            "metadata": chunk.get("metadata", {}),
   785→                        },
   786→                        f,
   787→                        ensure_ascii=False,
   788→                    )
   789→                    f.write("\n")
   790→                    offset_map[chunk["id"]] = offset
   791→
   792→            with open(offset_file, "wb") as f:
   793→                pickle.dump(offset_map, f)
   794→
   795→            server_manager: Optional[EmbeddingServerManager] = None
   796→            server_started = False
   797→            requested_zmq_port = int(os.getenv("LEANN_UPDATE_ZMQ_PORT", "5557"))
   798→
   799→            try:
   800→                if needs_recompute:
   801→                    server_manager = EmbeddingServerManager(
   802→                        backend_module_name="leann_backend_hnsw.hnsw_embedding_server"
   803→                    )
   804→                    server_started, actual_port = server_manager.start_server(
   805→                        port=requested_zmq_port,
   806→                        model_name=self.embedding_model,
   807→                        embedding_mode=passage_meta_mode,
   808→                        passages_file=str(meta_path),
   809→                        distance_metric=distance_metric,
   810→                        provider_options=passage_provider_options,
   811→                    )
   812→                    if not server_started:
   813→                        raise RuntimeError(
   814→                            "Failed to start HNSW embedding server for recompute update."
   815→                        )
   816→                    if actual_port != requested_zmq_port:
   817→                        logger.warning(
   818→                            "Embedding server started on port %s instead of requested %s. "
   819→                            "Using reassigned port.",
   820→                            actual_port,
   821→                            requested_zmq_port,
   822→                        )
   823→                    if hasattr(index.hnsw, "set_zmq_port"):
   824→                        index.hnsw.set_zmq_port(actual_port)
   825→                    elif hasattr(index, "set_zmq_port"):
   826→                        index.set_zmq_port(actual_port)
   827→
   828→                if needs_recompute:
   829→                    for i in range(embeddings.shape[0]):
   830→                        print(f"add {i} embeddings")
   831→                        index.add(1, faiss.swig_ptr(embeddings[i : i + 1]))
   832→                else:
   833→                    index.add(embeddings.shape[0], faiss.swig_ptr(embeddings))
   834→                faiss.write_index(index, str(index_file))
   835→            finally:
   836→                if server_started and server_manager is not None:
   837→                    server_manager.stop_server()
   838→
   839→        except Exception:
   840→            # Roll back appended passages/offset map to keep files consistent.
   841→            if passages_file.exists():
   842→                with open(passages_file, "rb+") as f:
   843→                    f.truncate(rollback_passages_size)
   844→            offset_map = offset_map_backup
   845→            with open(offset_file, "wb") as f:
   846→                pickle.dump(offset_map, f)
   847→            raise
   848→
   849→        meta["total_passages"] = len(offset_map)
   850→        with open(meta_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   851→            json.dump(meta, f, indent=2)
   852→
   853→        logger.info(
   854→            "Appended %d passages to index '%s'. New total: %d",
   855→            len(valid_chunks),
   856→            index_path,
   857→            len(offset_map),
   858→        )
   859→
   860→        self.chunks.clear()
   861→
   862→        if needs_recompute:

   906→    def search(
   907→        self,
   908→        query: str,
   909→        top_k: int = 5,
   910→        complexity: int = 64,
   911→        beam_width: int = 1,
   912→        prune_ratio: float = 0.0,
   913→        recompute_embeddings: bool = True,
   914→        pruning_strategy: Literal["global", "local", "proportional"] = "global",
   915→        expected_zmq_port: int = 5557,
   916→        metadata_filters: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, Union[str, int, float, bool, list]]]] = None,
   917→        batch_size: int = 0,
   918→        use_grep: bool = False,
   919→        provider_options: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
   920→        **kwargs,
   921→    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
   922→        """
   923→        Search for nearest neighbors with optional metadata filtering.
   924→
   925→        Args:
   926→            query: Text query to search for
   927→            top_k: Number of nearest neighbors to return
   928→            complexity: Search complexity/candidate list size, higher = more accurate but slower
   929→            beam_width: Number of parallel search paths/IO requests per iteration
   930→            prune_ratio: Ratio of neighbors to prune via approximate distance (0.0-1.0)
   931→            recompute_embeddings: Whether to fetch fresh embeddings from server vs use stored codes
   932→            pruning_strategy: Candidate selection strategy - "global" (default), "local", or "proportional"
   933→            expected_zmq_port: ZMQ port for embedding server communication
   934→            metadata_filters: Optional filters to apply to search results based on metadata.
   935→                Format: {"field_name": {"operator": value}}
   936→                Supported operators:
   937→                - Comparison: "==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="
   938→                - Membership: "in", "not_in"
   939→                - String: "contains", "starts_with", "ends_with"
   940→                Example: {"chapter": {"<=": 5}, "tags": {"in": ["fiction", "drama"]}}
   941→            **kwargs: Backend-specific parameters
   942→
   943→        Returns:
   944→            List of SearchResult objects with text, metadata, and similarity scores
   945→        """
   946→        # Handle grep search
   947→        if use_grep:
   948→            return self._grep_search(query, top_k)
   949→
   950→        logger.info("🔍 LeannSearcher.search() called:")
   951→        logger.info(f"  Query: '{query}'")
   952→        logger.info(f"  Top_k: {top_k}")
   953→        logger.info(f"  Metadata filters: {metadata_filters}")
   954→        logger.info(f"  Additional kwargs: {kwargs}")
   955→
   956→        # Smart top_k detection and adjustment
   957→        # Use PassageManager length (sum of shard sizes) to avoid
   958→        # depending on a massive combined map
   959→        total_docs = len(self.passage_manager)
   960→        original_top_k = top_k
   961→        if top_k > total_docs:
   962→            top_k = total_docs
   963→            logger.warning(
   964→                f"  ⚠️  Requested top_k ({original_top_k}) exceeds total documents ({total_docs})"
   965→            )
   966→            logger.warning(f"  ✅ Auto-adjusted top_k to {top_k} to match available documents")
   967→
   968→        zmq_port = None
   969→
   970→        start_time = time.time()
   971→        if recompute_embeddings:
   972→            zmq_port = self.backend_impl._ensure_server_running(
   973→                self.meta_path_str,
   974→                port=expected_zmq_port,
   975→                **kwargs,
   976→            )
   977→            del expected_zmq_port
   978→        zmq_time = time.time() - start_time
   979→        logger.info(f"  Launching server time: {zmq_time} seconds")
   980→
   981→        start_time = time.time()
   982→
   983→        # Extract query template from stored embedding_options with fallback chain:
   984→        # 1. Check provider_options override (highest priority)
   985→        # 2. Check query_prompt_template (new format)
   986→        # 3. Check prompt_template (old format for backward compat)
   987→        # 4. None (no template)
   988→        query_template = None
   989→        if provider_options and "prompt_template" in provider_options:
   990→            query_template = provider_options["prompt_template"]
   991→        elif "query_prompt_template" in self.embedding_options:
   992→            query_template = self.embedding_options["query_prompt_template"]
   993→        elif "prompt_template" in self.embedding_options:
   994→            query_template = self.embedding_options["prompt_template"]
   995→
   996→        query_embedding = self.backend_impl.compute_query_embedding(
   997→            query,
   998→            use_server_if_available=recompute_embeddings,
   999→            zmq_port=zmq_port,
  1000→            query_template=query_template,
  1001→        )
  1002→        logger.info(f"  Generated embedding shape: {query_embedding.shape}")
  1003→        embedding_time = time.time() - start_time
  1004→        logger.info(f"  Embedding time: {embedding_time} seconds")
  1005→
  1006→        start_time = time.time()
  1007→        backend_search_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
  1008→            "complexity": complexity,
  1009→            "beam_width": beam_width,
  1010→            "prune_ratio": prune_ratio,
  1011→            "recompute_embeddings": recompute_embeddings,
  1012→            "pruning_strategy": pruning_strategy,
  1013→            "zmq_port": zmq_port,
  1014→        }
  1015→        # Only HNSW supports batching; forward conditionally
  1016→        if self.backend_name == "hnsw":
  1017→            backend_search_kwargs["batch_size"] = batch_size
  1018→
  1019→        # Merge any extra kwargs last
  1020→        backend_search_kwargs.update(kwargs)
  1021→
  1022→        results = self.backend_impl.search(
  1023→            query_embedding,
  1024→            top_k,
  1025→            **backend_search_kwargs,
  1026→        )
  1027→        search_time = time.time() - start_time
  1028→        logger.info(f"  Search time in search() LEANN searcher: {search_time} seconds")
  1029→        logger.info(f"  Backend returned: labels={len(results.get('labels', [[]])[0])} results")
  1030→
  1031→        enriched_results = []
  1032→        if "labels" in results and "distances" in results:
  1033→            logger.info(f"  Processing {len(results['labels'][0])} passage IDs:")
  1034→            # Python 3.9 does not support zip(strict=...); lengths are expected to match
  1035→            for i, (string_id, dist) in enumerate(
  1036→                zip(results["labels"][0], results["distances"][0])
  1037→            ):
  1038→                try:
  1039→                    passage_data = self.passage_manager.get_passage(string_id)
  1040→                    enriched_results.append(
  1041→                        SearchResult(
  1042→                            id=string_id,
  1043→                            score=dist,
  1044→                            text=passage_data["text"],
  1045→                            metadata=passage_data.get("metadata", {}),
  1046→                        )
  1047→                    )
  1048→
  1049→                    # Color codes for better logging
  1050→                    GREEN = "\033[92m"
  1051→                    BLUE = "\033[94m"
  1052→                    YELLOW = "\033[93m"
  1053→                    RESET = "\033[0m"
  1054→
  1055→                    # Truncate text for display (first 100 chars)
  1056→                    display_text = passage_data["text"]
  1057→                    logger.info(
  1058→                        f"   {GREEN}✓{RESET} {BLUE}[{i + 1:2d}]{RESET} {YELLOW}ID:{RESET} '{string_id}' {YELLOW}Score:{RESET} {dist:.4f} {YELLOW}Text:{RESET} {display_text}"
  1059→                    )
  1060→                except KeyError:
  1061→                    RED = "\033[91m"
  1062→                    RESET = "\033[0m"
  1063→                    logger.error(
  1064→                        f"   {RED}✗{RESET} [{i + 1:2d}] ID: '{string_id}' -> {RED}ERROR: Passage not found!{RESET}"
  1065→                    )
  1066→
  1067→        # Apply metadata filters if specified
  1068→        if metadata_filters:
  1069→            logger.info(f"  🔍 Applying metadata filters: {metadata_filters}")
  1070→            enriched_results = self.passage_manager.filter_search_results(
  1071→                enriched_results, metadata_filters
  1072→            )
  1073→
  1074→        # Define color codes outside the loop for final message
  1075→        GREEN = "\033[92m"
  1076→        RESET = "\033[0m"
  1077→        logger.info(f"  {GREEN}✓ Final enriched results: {len(enriched_results)} passages{RESET}")
  1078→        return enriched_results

  1080→    def _find_jsonl_file(self) -> Optional[str]:
  1081→        """Find the .jsonl file containing raw passages for grep search"""
  1082→        index_path = Path(self.meta_path_str).parent
  1083→        potential_files = [
  1084→            index_path / "documents.leann.passages.jsonl",
  1085→            index_path.parent / "documents.leann.passages.jsonl",
  1086→        ]
  1087→
  1088→        for file_path in potential_files:
  1089→            if file_path.exists():
  1090→                return str(file_path)
  1091→        return None

  1093→    def _grep_search(self, query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> list[SearchResult]:
  1094→        """Perform grep-based search on raw passages"""
  1095→        jsonl_file = self._find_jsonl_file()
  1096→        if not jsonl_file:
  1097→            raise FileNotFoundError("No .jsonl passages file found for grep search")
  1098→
  1099→        try:
  1100→            cmd = ["grep", "-i", "-n", query, jsonl_file]
  1101→            result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
  1102→
  1103→            if result.returncode == 1:
  1104→                return []
  1105→            elif result.returncode != 0:
  1106→                raise RuntimeError(f"Grep failed: {result.stderr}")
  1107→
  1108→            matches = []
  1109→            for line in result.stdout.strip().split("\n"):
  1110→                if not line:
  1111→                    continue
  1112→                parts = line.split(":", 1)
  1113→                if len(parts) != 2:
  1114→                    continue
  1115→
  1116→                try:
  1117→                    data = json.loads(parts[1])
  1118→                    text = data.get("text", "")
  1119→                    score = text.lower().count(query.lower())
  1120→
  1121→                    matches.append(
  1122→                        SearchResult(
  1123→                            id=data.get("id", parts[0]),
  1124→                            text=text,
  1125→                            metadata=data.get("metadata", {}),
  1126→                            score=float(score),
  1127→                        )
  1128→                    )
  1129→                except json.JSONDecodeError:
  1130→                    continue
  1131→
  1132→            matches.sort(key=lambda x: x.score, reverse=True)
  1133→            return matches[:top_k]
  1134→
  1135→        except FileNotFoundError:
  1136→            raise RuntimeError(
  1137→                "grep command not found. Please install grep or use semantic search."
  1138→            )

  1140→    def _python_regex_search(self, query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> list[SearchResult]:
  1141→        """Fallback regex search"""
  1142→        jsonl_file = self._find_jsonl_file()
  1143→        if not jsonl_file:
  1144→            raise FileNotFoundError("No .jsonl file found")
  1145→
  1146→        pattern = re.compile(re.escape(query), re.IGNORECASE)
  1147→        matches = []
  1148→
  1149→        with open(jsonl_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
  1150→            for line_num, line in enumerate(f, 1):
  1151→                if pattern.search(line):
  1152→                    try:
  1153→                        data = json.loads(line.strip())
  1154→                        matches.append(
  1155→                            SearchResult(
  1156→                                id=data.get("id", str(line_num)),
  1157→                                text=data.get("text", ""),
  1158→                                metadata=data.get("metadata", {}),
  1159→                                score=float(len(pattern.findall(data.get("text", "")))),
  1160→                            )
  1161→                        )
  1162→                    except json.JSONDecodeError:
  1163→                        continue
  1164→
  1165→        matches.sort(key=lambda x: x.score, reverse=True)
  1166→        return matches[:top_k]

1→"""
     2→Metadata filtering engine for LEANN search results.
     3→
     4→This module provides generic metadata filtering capabilities that can be applied
     5→to search results from any LEANN backend. The filtering supports various
     6→operators for different data types including numbers, strings, booleans, and lists.
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→from typing import Any, Optional, Union
    11→
    12→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    13→
    14→# Type alias for filter specifications
    15→FilterValue = Union[str, int, float, bool, list]
    16→FilterSpec = dict[str, FilterValue]
    17→MetadataFilters = dict[str, FilterSpec]
    18→
    19→
    20→class MetadataFilterEngine:
    21→    """
    22→    Engine for evaluating metadata filters against search results.
    23→
    24→    Supports various operators for filtering based on metadata fields:
    25→    - Comparison: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=
    26→    - Membership: in, not_in
    27→    - String operations: contains, starts_with, ends_with
    28→    - Boolean operations: is_true, is_false
    29→    """
    30→
    31→    def __init__(self):
    32→        """Initialize the filter engine with supported operators."""
    33→        self.operators = {
    34→            "==": self._equals,
    35→            "!=": self._not_equals,
    36→            "<": self._less_than,
    37→            "<=": self._less_than_or_equal,
    38→            ">": self._greater_than,
    39→            ">=": self._greater_than_or_equal,
    40→            "in": self._in,
    41→            "not_in": self._not_in,
    42→            "contains": self._contains,
    43→            "starts_with": self._starts_with,
    44→            "ends_with": self._ends_with,
    45→            "is_true": self._is_true,
    46→            "is_false": self._is_false,
    47→        }
    48→
    49→    def apply_filters(
    50→        self, search_results: list[dict[str, Any]], metadata_filters: Optional[MetadataFilters]
    51→    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    52→        """
    53→        Apply metadata filters to a list of search results.
    54→
    55→        Args:
    56→            search_results: List of result dictionaries, each containing 'metadata' field
    57→            metadata_filters: Dictionary of filter specifications
    58→                Format: {"field_name": {"operator": value}}
    59→
    60→        Returns:
    61→            Filtered list of search results
    62→        """
    63→        if not metadata_filters:
    64→            return search_results
    65→
    66→        logger.debug(f"Applying filters: {metadata_filters}")
    67→        logger.debug(f"Input results count: {len(search_results)}")
    68→
    69→        filtered_results = []
    70→        for result in search_results:
    71→            if self._evaluate_filters(result, metadata_filters):
    72→                filtered_results.append(result)
    73→
    74→        logger.debug(f"Filtered results count: {len(filtered_results)}")
    75→        return filtered_results
    76→
    77→    def _evaluate_filters(self, result: dict[str, Any], filters: MetadataFilters) -> bool:
    78→        """
    79→        Evaluate all filters against a single search result.
    80→
    81→        All filters must pass (AND logic) for the result to be included.
    82→
    83→        Args:
    84→            result: Full search result dictionary (including metadata, text, etc.)
    85→            filters: Filter specifications to evaluate
    86→
    87→        Returns:
    88→            True if all filters pass, False otherwise
    89→        """
    90→        for field_name, filter_spec in filters.items():
    91→            if not self._evaluate_field_filter(result, field_name, filter_spec):
    92→                return False
    93→        return True
    94→
    95→    def _evaluate_field_filter(
    96→        self, result: dict[str, Any], field_name: str, filter_spec: FilterSpec
    97→    ) -> bool:
    98→        """
    99→        Evaluate a single field filter against a search result.
   100→
   101→        Args:
   102→            result: Full search result dictionary
   103→            field_name: Name of the field to filter on
   104→            filter_spec: Filter specification for this field
   105→
   106→        Returns:
   107→            True if the filter passes, False otherwise
   108→        """
   109→        # First check top-level fields, then check metadata
   110→        field_value = result.get(field_name)
   111→        if field_value is None:
   112→            # Try to get from metadata if not found at top level
   113→            metadata = result.get("metadata", {})
   114→            field_value = metadata.get(field_name)
   115→
   116→        # Handle missing fields - they fail all filters except existence checks
   117→        if field_value is None:
   118→            logger.debug(f"Field '{field_name}' not found in result or metadata")
   119→            return False
   120→
   121→        # Evaluate each operator in the filter spec
   122→        for operator, expected_value in filter_spec.items():
   123→            if operator not in self.operators:
   124→                logger.warning(f"Unsupported operator: {operator}")
   125→                return False
   126→
   127→            try:
   128→                if not self.operators[operator](field_value, expected_value):
   129→                    logger.debug(
   130→                        f"Filter failed: {field_name} {operator} {expected_value} "
   131→                        f"(actual: {field_value})"
   132→                    )
   133→                    return False
   134→            except Exception as e:
   135→                logger.warning(
   136→                    f"Error evaluating filter {field_name} {operator} {expected_value}: {e}"
   137→                )
   138→                return False
   139→
   140→        return True
   141→
   142→    # Comparison operators
   143→    def _equals(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   144→        """Check if field value equals expected value."""
   145→        return field_value == expected_value
   146→
   147→    def _not_equals(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   148→        """Check if field value does not equal expected value."""
   149→        return field_value != expected_value
   150→
   151→    def _less_than(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   152→        """Check if field value is less than expected value."""
   153→        return self._numeric_compare(field_value, expected_value, lambda a, b: a < b)
   154→
   155→    def _less_than_or_equal(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   156→        """Check if field value is less than or equal to expected value."""
   157→        return self._numeric_compare(field_value, expected_value, lambda a, b: a <= b)
   158→
   159→    def _greater_than(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   160→        """Check if field value is greater than expected value."""
   161→        return self._numeric_compare(field_value, expected_value, lambda a, b: a > b)
   162→
   163→    def _greater_than_or_equal(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   164→        """Check if field value is greater than or equal to expected value."""
   165→        return self._numeric_compare(field_value, expected_value, lambda a, b: a >= b)
   166→
   167→    # Membership operators
   168→    def _in(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   169→        """Check if field value is in the expected list/collection."""
   170→        if not isinstance(expected_value, (list, tuple, set)):
   171→            raise ValueError("'in' operator requires a list, tuple, or set")
   172→        return field_value in expected_value
   173→
   174→    def _not_in(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   175→        """Check if field value is not in the expected list/collection."""
   176→        if not isinstance(expected_value, (list, tuple, set)):
   177→            raise ValueError("'not_in' operator requires a list, tuple, or set")
   178→        return field_value not in expected_value
   179→
   180→    # String operators
   181→    def _contains(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   182→        """Check if field value contains the expected substring."""
   183→        field_str = str(field_value)
   184→        expected_str = str(expected_value)
   185→        return expected_str in field_str
   186→
   187→    def _starts_with(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   188→        """Check if field value starts with the expected prefix."""
   189→        field_str = str(field_value)
   190→        expected_str = str(expected_value)
   191→        return field_str.startswith(expected_str)
   192→
   193→    def _ends_with(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   194→        """Check if field value ends with the expected suffix."""
   195→        field_str = str(field_value)
   196→        expected_str = str(expected_value)
   197→        return field_str.endswith(expected_str)
   198→
   199→    # Boolean operators
   200→    def _is_true(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   201→        """Check if field value is truthy."""
   202→        return bool(field_value)
   203→
   204→    def _is_false(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any) -> bool:
   205→        """Check if field value is falsy."""
   206→        return not bool(field_value)
   207→
   208→    # Helper methods
   209→    def _numeric_compare(self, field_value: Any, expected_value: Any, compare_func) -> bool:
   210→        """
   211→        Helper for numeric comparisons with type coercion.
   212→
   213→        Args:
   214→            field_value: Value from metadata
   215→            expected_value: Value to compare against
   216→            compare_func: Comparison function to apply
   217→
   218→        Returns:
   219→            Result of comparison
   220→        """
   221→        try:
   222→            # Try to convert both values to numbers for comparison
   223→            if isinstance(field_value, str) and isinstance(expected_value, str):
   224→                # String comparison if both are strings
   225→                return compare_func(field_value, expected_value)
   226→
   227→            # Numeric comparison - attempt to convert to float
   228→            field_num = (
   229→                float(field_value) if not isinstance(field_value, (int, float)) else field_value
   230→            )
   231→            expected_num = (
   232→                float(expected_value)
   233→                if not isinstance(expected_value, (int, float))
   234→                else expected_value
   235→            )
   236→
   237→            return compare_func(field_num, expected_num)
   238→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   239→            # Fall back to string comparison if numeric conversion fails
   240→            return compare_func(str(field_value), str(expected_value))
   241→

   644→    def update_index(self, index_path: str):

    61→    if chunking_mode == "traditional":
    62→        # Traditional chunking uses tokens
    63→        # Max chunk = chunk_size + overlap, so chunk_size = limit - overlap
    64→        return max(1, safe_limit - overlap_tokens)
    65→    else:  # AST chunking
    66→        # AST uses characters, need to convert
    67→        # Conservative estimate: 1.2 tokens per char for code
    68→        overlap_chars = int(overlap_tokens * 3)  # ~3 chars per token for code
    69→        safe_chars = int(safe_limit / 1.2)
    70→        return max(1, safe_chars - overlap_chars)

    72→
    73→def validate_chunk_token_limits(chunks: list[str], max_tokens: int = 512) -> tuple[list[str], int]:
    74→    """
    75→    Validate that chunks don't exceed token limits and truncate if necessary.
    76→
    77→    Args:
    78→        chunks: List of text chunks to validate
    79→        max_tokens: Maximum tokens allowed per chunk
    80→
    81→    Returns:
    82→        Tuple of (validated_chunks, num_truncated)
    83→    """
    84→    validated_chunks = []
    85→    num_truncated = 0
    86→
    87→    for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks):
    88→        estimated_tokens = estimate_token_count(chunk)
    89→
    90→        if estimated_tokens > max_tokens:
    91→            # Truncate chunk to fit token limit
    92→            try:
    93→                import tiktoken
    94→
    95→                encoder = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
    96→                tokens = encoder.encode(chunk)
    97→                if len(tokens) > max_tokens:
    98→                    truncated_tokens = tokens[:max_tokens]
    99→                    truncated_chunk = encoder.decode(truncated_tokens)
   100→                    validated_chunks.append(truncated_chunk)
   101→                    num_truncated += 1
   102→                    logger.warning(
   103→                        f"Truncated chunk {i} from {len(tokens)} to {max_tokens} tokens "
   104→                        f"(from {len(chunk)} to {len(truncated_chunk)} characters)"
   105→                    )
   106→                else:
   107→                    validated_chunks.append(chunk)
   108→            except ImportError:
   109→                # Fallback: Conservative character truncation
   110→                char_limit = int(max_tokens / 1.2)  # Conservative for code
   111→                if len(chunk) > char_limit:
   112→                    truncated_chunk = chunk[:char_limit]
   113→                    validated_chunks.append(truncated_chunk)
   114→                    num_truncated += 1
   115→                    logger.warning(
   116→                        f"Truncated chunk {i} from {len(chunk)} to {char_limit} characters "
   117→                        f"(conservative estimate for {max_tokens} tokens)"
   118→                    )
   119→                else:
   120→                    validated_chunks.append(chunk)
   121→        else:
   122→            validated_chunks.append(chunk)
   123→
   124→    if num_truncated > 0:
   125→        logger.warning(f"Truncated {num_truncated}/{len(chunks)} chunks to fit token limits")
   126→
   127→    return validated_chunks, num_truncated

   130→# Code file extensions supported by astchunk
   131→CODE_EXTENSIONS = {
   132→    ".py": "python",
   133→    ".java": "java",
   134→    ".cs": "csharp",
   135→    ".ts": "typescript",
   136→    ".tsx": "typescript",
   137→    ".js": "typescript",
   138→    ".jsx": "typescript",

   142→def detect_code_files(documents, code_extensions=None) -> tuple[list, list]:
   143→    """Separate documents into code files and regular text files."""
   144→    if code_extensions is None:
   145→        code_extensions = CODE_EXTENSIONS
   146→
   147→    code_docs = []
   148→    text_docs = []
   149→
   150→    for doc in documents:
   151→        file_path = doc.metadata.get("file_path", "") or doc.metadata.get("file_name", "")
   152→        if file_path:
   153→            file_ext = Path(file_path).suffix.lower()
   154→            if file_ext in code_extensions:
   155→                doc.metadata["language"] = code_extensions[file_ext]
   156→                doc.metadata["is_code"] = True
   157→                code_docs.append(doc)
   158→            else:
   159→                doc.metadata["is_code"] = False
   160→                text_docs.append(doc)
   161→        else:
   162→            doc.metadata["is_code"] = False
   163→            text_docs.append(doc)
   164→
   165→    logger.info(f"Detected {len(code_docs)} code files and {len(text_docs)} text files")
   166→    return code_docs, text_docs

   169→def get_language_from_extension(file_path: str) -> Optional[str]:
   170→    """Return language string from a filename/extension using CODE_EXTENSIONS."""
   171→    ext = Path(file_path).suffix.lower()
   172→    return CODE_EXTENSIONS.get(ext)
   173→

   175→def create_ast_chunks(
   176→    documents,
   177→    max_chunk_size: int = 512,
   178→    chunk_overlap: int = 64,
   179→    metadata_template: str = "default",
   180→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   181→    """Create AST-aware chunks from code documents using astchunk.
   182→
   183→    Falls back to traditional chunking if astchunk is unavailable.
   184→
   185→    Returns:
   186→        List of dicts with {"text": str, "metadata": dict}
   187→    """
   188→    try:
   189→        from astchunk import ASTChunkBuilder  # optional dependency
   190→    except ImportError as e:
   191→        logger.error(f"astchunk not available: {e}")
   192→        logger.info("Falling back to traditional chunking for code files")
   193→        return _traditional_chunks_as_dicts(documents, max_chunk_size, chunk_overlap)
   194→
   195→    all_chunks = []
   196→    for doc in documents:
   197→        language = doc.metadata.get("language")
   198→        if not language:
   199→            logger.warning("No language detected; falling back to traditional chunking")
   200→            all_chunks.extend(_traditional_chunks_as_dicts([doc], max_chunk_size, chunk_overlap))
   201→            continue
   202→
   203→        try:
   204→            # Warn once if AST chunk size + overlap might exceed common token limits
   205→            # Note: Actual truncation happens at embedding time with dynamic model limits
   206→            global _ast_token_warning_shown
   207→            estimated_max_tokens = int(
   208→                (max_chunk_size + chunk_overlap) * 1.2
   209→            )  # Conservative estimate
   210→            if estimated_max_tokens > 512 and not _ast_token_warning_shown:
   211→                logger.warning(
   212→                    f"AST chunk size ({max_chunk_size}) + overlap ({chunk_overlap}) = {max_chunk_size + chunk_overlap} chars "
   213→                    f"may exceed 512 token limit (~{estimated_max_tokens} tokens estimated). "
   214→                    f"Consider reducing --ast-chunk-size to {int(400 / 1.2)} or --ast-chunk-overlap to {int(50 / 1.2)}. "
   215→                    f"Note: Chunks will be auto-truncated at embedding time based on your model's actual token limit."
   216→                )
   217→                _ast_token_warning_shown = True
   218→
   219→            configs = {
   220→                "max_chunk_size": max_chunk_size,
   221→                "language": language,
   222→                "metadata_template": metadata_template,
   223→                "chunk_overlap": chunk_overlap if chunk_overlap > 0 else 0,
   224→            }
   225→
   226→            repo_metadata = {
   227→                "file_path": doc.metadata.get("file_path", ""),
   228→                "file_name": doc.metadata.get("file_name", ""),
   229→                "creation_date": doc.metadata.get("creation_date", ""),
   230→                "last_modified_date": doc.metadata.get("last_modified_date", ""),
   231→            }
   232→            configs["repo_level_metadata"] = repo_metadata
   233→
   234→            chunk_builder = ASTChunkBuilder(**configs)
   235→            code_content = doc.get_content()
   236→            if not code_content or not code_content.strip():
   237→                logger.warning("Empty code content, skipping")
   238→                continue
   239→
   240→            chunks = chunk_builder.chunkify(code_content)
   241→            for chunk in chunks:
   242→                chunk_text: str | None = None
   243→                astchunk_metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}
   244→
   245→                if hasattr(chunk, "text"):
   246→                    chunk_text = str(chunk.text) if chunk.text else None
   247→                elif isinstance(chunk, str):
   248→                    chunk_text = chunk
   249→                elif isinstance(chunk, dict):
   250→                    # Handle astchunk format: {"content": "...", "metadata": {...}}
   251→                    if "content" in chunk:
   252→                        chunk_text = chunk["content"]
   253→                        astchunk_metadata = chunk.get("metadata", {})
   254→                    elif "text" in chunk:
   255→                        chunk_text = chunk["text"]
   256→                    else:
   257→                        chunk_text = str(chunk)  # Last resort
   258→                else:
   259→                    chunk_text = str(chunk)
   260→
   261→                if chunk_text and chunk_text.strip():
   262→                    # Extract document-level metadata
   263→                    doc_metadata = {
   264→                        "file_path": doc.metadata.get("file_path", ""),
   265→                        "file_name": doc.metadata.get("file_name", ""),
   266→                    }
   267→                    if "creation_date" in doc.metadata:
   268→                        doc_metadata["creation_date"] = doc.metadata["creation_date"]
   269→                    if "last_modified_date" in doc.metadata:
   270→                        doc_metadata["last_modified_date"] = doc.metadata["last_modified_date"]
   271→
   272→                    # Merge document metadata + astchunk metadata
   273→                    combined_metadata = {**doc_metadata, **astchunk_metadata}
   274→
   275→                    all_chunks.append({"text": chunk_text.strip(), "metadata": combined_metadata})
   276→
   277→            logger.info(
   278→                f"Created {len(chunks)} AST chunks from {language} file: {doc.metadata.get('file_name', 'unknown')}"
   279→            )
   280→        except Exception as e:
   281→            logger.warning(f"AST chunking failed for {language} file: {e}")
   282→            logger.info("Falling back to traditional chunking")
   283→            all_chunks.extend(_traditional_chunks_as_dicts([doc], max_chunk_size, chunk_overlap))
   284→

   287→
   288→def create_traditional_chunks(
   289→    documents, chunk_size: int = 256, chunk_overlap: int = 128
   290→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   291→    """Create traditional text chunks using LlamaIndex SentenceSplitter.
   292→
   293→    Returns:
   294→        List of dicts with {"text": str, "metadata": dict}
   295→    """
   296→    if chunk_size <= 0:
   297→        logger.warning(f"Invalid chunk_size={chunk_size}, using default value of 256")
   298→        chunk_size = 256
   299→    if chunk_overlap < 0:
   300→        chunk_overlap = 0
   301→    if chunk_overlap >= chunk_size:
   302→        chunk_overlap = chunk_size // 2
   303→
   304→    node_parser = SentenceSplitter(
   305→        chunk_size=chunk_size,
   306→        chunk_overlap=chunk_overlap,
   307→        separator=" ",
   308→        paragraph_separator="\n\n",
   309→    )
   310→
   311→    result = []
   312→    for doc in documents:
   313→        # Extract document-level metadata
   314→        doc_metadata = {
   315→            "file_path": doc.metadata.get("file_path", ""),
   316→            "file_name": doc.metadata.get("file_name", ""),
   317→        }
   318→        if "creation_date" in doc.metadata:
   319→            doc_metadata["creation_date"] = doc.metadata["creation_date"]
   320→        if "last_modified_date" in doc.metadata:
   321→            doc_metadata["last_modified_date"] = doc.metadata["last_modified_date"]
   322→
   323→        try:
   324→            nodes = node_parser.get_nodes_from_documents([doc])
   325→            if nodes:
   326→                for node in nodes:
   327→                    result.append({"text": node.get_content(), "metadata": doc_metadata})
   328→        except Exception as e:
   329→            logger.error(f"Traditional chunking failed for document: {e}")
   330→            content = doc.get_content()
   331→            if content and content.strip():
   332→                result.append({"text": content.strip(), "metadata": doc_metadata})
   333→
   334→    return result

   337→def _traditional_chunks_as_dicts(
   338→    documents, chunk_size: int = 256, chunk_overlap: int = 128
   339→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   340→    """Helper: Traditional chunking that returns dict format for consistency.
   341→
   342→    This is now just an alias for create_traditional_chunks for backwards compatibility.
   343→    """
   344→    return create_traditional_chunks(documents, chunk_size, chunk_overlap)
   345→
   346→
   347→def create_text_chunks(
   348→    documents,
   349→    chunk_size: int = 256,
   350→    chunk_overlap: int = 128,
   351→    use_ast_chunking: bool = False,
   352→    ast_chunk_size: int = 512,
   353→    ast_chunk_overlap: int = 64,
   354→    code_file_extensions: Optional[list[str]] = None,
   355→    ast_fallback_traditional: bool = True,
   356→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   357→    """Create text chunks from documents with optional AST support for code files.
   358→
   359→    Returns:
   360→        List of dicts with {"text": str, "metadata": dict}
   361→    """
   362→    if not documents:
   363→        logger.warning("No documents provided for chunking")
   364→        return []
   365→
   366→    local_code_extensions = CODE_EXTENSIONS.copy()
   367→    if code_file_extensions:
   368→        ext_mapping = {
   369→            ".py": "python",
   370→            ".java": "java",
   371→            ".cs": "c_sharp",
   372→            ".ts": "typescript",
   373→            ".tsx": "typescript",
   374→        }
   375→        for ext in code_file_extensions:
   376→            if ext.lower() not in local_code_extensions:
   377→                if ext.lower() in ext_mapping:
   378→                    local_code_extensions[ext.lower()] = ext_mapping[ext.lower()]
   379→                else:
   380→                    logger.warning(f"Unsupported extension {ext}, will use traditional chunking")
   381→
   382→    all_chunks = []
   383→    if use_ast_chunking:
   384→        code_docs, text_docs = detect_code_files(documents, local_code_extensions)
   385→        if code_docs:
   386→            try:
   387→                all_chunks.extend(
   388→                    create_ast_chunks(
   389→                        code_docs, max_chunk_size=ast_chunk_size, chunk_overlap=ast_chunk_overlap
   390→                    )
   391→                )
   392→            except Exception as e:
   393→                logger.error(f"AST chunking failed: {e}")
   394→                if ast_fallback_traditional:
   395→                    all_chunks.extend(
   396→                        _traditional_chunks_as_dicts(code_docs, chunk_size, chunk_overlap)
   397→                    )
   398→                else:
   399→                    raise
   400→        if text_docs:
   401→            all_chunks.extend(_traditional_chunks_as_dicts(text_docs, chunk_size, chunk_overlap))
   402→    else:
   403→        all_chunks = _traditional_chunks_as_dicts(documents, chunk_size, chunk_overlap)
   404→
   405→    logger.info(f"Total chunks created: {len(all_chunks)}")
   406→
   407→    # Note: Token truncation is now handled at embedding time with dynamic model limits
   408→    # See get_model_token_limit() and truncate_to_token_limit() in embedding_compute.py
   409→    return all_chunks
